local_articles.snippet: NEW YORK, July 7 - France's World Cup campaign has already tested their firepower, patience and nerves, but Thursday's quarter-final against Morocco will offer Didier Deschamps' side something different: their first full football examination of the tournament. questions.title: Who will FIFA appoint to referee the 2026 men's World Cup final?
questions.background: The final is scheduled for July 19, 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : FIFA's official appointment for the men's World Cup final on July 19, 2026, as announced before kickoff. Resolve to the main on-field referee named in that appointment. Resolution Date : 2026-07-19 Accepted Answer Format : The referee's full name (string).
questions.current_reasoning: FIFA selected 52 referees (51 active after Artan's US entry refusal) under Pierluigi Collina, with zero referees ever repeating a World Cup final (effectively excluding 2022 final ref Szymon Marciniak) and strict nationality/confederation neutrality disqualifying refs whose countries reach the final. Historically, every WC final referee since 1990 was aged 38-43 and held elite major-final pedigree; in 2026, ~45% of finals project to be UEFA-vs-UEFA and ~44% UEFA-vs-CONMEBOL. István Kovács (Romania, age 41, 2025 UCL Final, zero country conflict) and Slavko Vinčić (Slovenia, age 46, 2024 UCL Final, zero country conflict) lead UEFA's neutral tier, Ismail Elfath (USA, age 44, 2022 WC Final 4th official) and César Arturo Ramos (Mexico, age 42, 2022 WC Semifinal ref) lead CONCACAF neutrals, and Clément Turpin (France, age 44, 2022 UCL Final) leads French contenders though discounted for France's ~35-40% SF/Final risk; with 51 officials still active on June 24, 59% of mass properly remains on the field (Letexier, Valenzuela, Claus, Faghani, Sampaio, Makkelie, Tello, etc.).
